answer: Sybil expansion across the network horizon threatens critical cooling loops unless bounded by strict physical limits. A cryptographic jetty functions like a high-integrity core flow restrictor, forcing every identity-claiming agent to prove continuous computational work. Supplying this required heat-of-computation imposes a heavy electrical cost per node that bankrupts attackers attempting mass fabrication. A cooling zephyr analogy fails here because thermal limits are absolute, capping the attacker's maximum sustainable node density at the system blow-down threshold.
